https://www.forbes.ro/brian-mac-mahon-di.text: Romania no longer has an entrepreneurial mindset problem, but rather the risk of losing its entrepreneurs to other countries. This is the conclusion of Brian Mac Mahon, Director at Nathan Family Office and founder of Expert DOJO, who spoke at Forbes România Business Bridges 2026, the event organized by Forbes Romania at Forbes on Fifth in New York. "The mindset is not the problem. What we don't want to happen is to lose these great entrepreneurs to other countries. When you build bridges, they are about maintaining the incredible innovation at home, but then bridging into places where that innovation can fully flourish," Brian Mac Mahon said. Until recently, his diagnosis for European entrepreneurs was an excess of logic. "What America has is this ability to embrace the impossible, not even expecting it to be possible, but just expecting it to be a little bit less impossible. For us Europeans, it's not logical. The simple thing that's always held Europeans back, Romanians, Irish, everybody else, is that we're too logical in how we approach things," he explained. Irish by origin, Mac Mahon came to the United States many years ago, became a director at Nathan Family Office, a multi-billion-dollar family office based in California, and later a partner in it. The office owns significant real estate in the San Francisco area, but has completely changed its strategy. "We haven't made an investment in real estate for the last seven, eight years. Instead, we have become one of the most prolific venture capital investors in the world, with over 300 investments over that period, because we recognized what was happening now and what the opportunity was," the investor said. "In the world today, there are over 800 unicorns, billion-dollar companies which are still growing. Twenty years ago, there were only 13," Mac Mahon noted. "This isn't just about Romania helping entrepreneurs because it's good for entrepreneurs. This is about Romania becoming a world power by harnessing the full force of these companies and where they are going. Because it's not going to stop. It's going to keep on growing at an unparalleled rate," he said. For the next decade, the investor sees three priorities: educating children, training entrepreneurs, and a bridge that works both ways, with the diaspora involved in building companies at home. "I really hope that over the next three, five, ten years, I'll see Romania really embrace this era of entrepreneurship: how we educate our kids, how we train these great entrepreneurs to build some of the biggest companies in the world," Brian Mac Mahon concluded.

https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/nato-scra.text: Paul Withers Updated Sat, October 10, 2026 at 2:21 PM UTC 28 F-18 fighter jets were scrambled overnight (Image: Getty) NATO has been forced to rapidly scramble more fighter jets again following a huge overnight Russian drone attack on Ukraine, sparking more fears a possible World War 3 could break out. Vladimir Putin's forces have unleashed relentless attacks on Ukraine over recent days. Residential buildings have been reduced to rubble , with several people killed. Russia launched more attacks on Ukraine overnight, which saw NATO scramble fighter jets again. The Romanain Ministry of Defence (MoD) said its radar surveillance system "detected an air target evolving in Ukrainian airspace", about 20km north of Periprava, near the border with Romania. Two F-18 aircraft of the Spanish Air and Space Forces were subsequently scambled. The Romanian MoD said: "On the night of October 9 to 10, the radar surveillance system of the Ministry of National Defense detected an air target evolving in Ukrainian airspace, about 20 km north of Periprava, near the border with Romania. Two F-18 aircraft of the Spanish Air and Space Forces, in the Reinforced Air Police combat service, took off from the 57th Mihail Koglniceanu Air Base. The National Military Command Center notified the General Inspectorate for Emergency Situations about the establishment of measures to alert the population in the north of Tulcea County, and at 00:17 a RO-Alert message was sent. The air alert ceased at 00.40." However, the Romanian MoD said a "new air target evolving in Ukrainian airspace, in the area of Chilia, about 15km east of Valcove", was identified. It added: "At 02.18, a new RO-Alert message was sent to the population in the north of Tulcea County. The air alert ceased at 03.13. No penetrations into the national airspace were detected." Putin's forces have ramped up their brutal attacks on Ukraine (Image: Getty) It came after it emerged that people were possibly trapped under rubble, with five killed and 10 injured, following a Russian airstrike in Zaporizhzhia. Acting Governor Mykhailo Semikin wrote in a post on Telegram: "The death toll from this morning's Russian attack on Zaporizhzhia has risen to five. Among them are two children. "Ten more people were injured. Search and rescue operations are ongoing at the sites of the strikes. People may still be trapped under the rubble. Our deepest condolences go out to the families and loved ones of those who died." Last week, NATO fighter jets were scrambled in Lithuania after a suspected drone crossed into the country, forcing the capital city's main airport to close its airspace. Lithuanian authorities issued a possible air threat alert to residents, urging them to find a safe place. The suspected drone was detected entering Lithuania's airspace from Belarus last Saturday morning, sparking an alert that was sounded shortly before 10am local time. However, about 40 minutes later, the alert was stood down. Vilmantas Vitkauskas, head of Lithuania's National Crisis Management Centre, said the object had moved away from the NATO ally's observation zone.
